title: Analysis of pistachio shell-derived activated porous carbon materials for hydrogen adsorption
material_description: ACNC10-900 | pistachio-shell carbon chemically activated with 10 % (w/w) NaCl and carbonized at 900 C for 30 min under N2; nitrogen-containing (authors: self-nitrogen doping)
purification_method: shells washed with DI water and ethanol, dried (80 C 8 h; air 1 day; 120 C 2 h) and ground before activation; carbonized product washed and dried
activation_method: one-step: shells soaked 1 day in 10 % (w/w) NaCl, air-dried 3 days, then carbonized in a sealed crucible in a tube furnace under N2, 10 C/min to 900 C, held 30 min
source_location: main, p. 266 (main-07), Fig. 9, ACNC10-900 series (grey squares), adsorption branch
notes: archive: fig9_ACNC10-900.json; digitized 35.034 kPa, 0.8066 mmol/g (pressure axis in kPa, converted to bar). Fig. 9 isotherm measured on the Micromeritics ASAP 2020 (77 K, up to 120 kPa). isotherm_point_count left empty: the low-pressure adsorption branch (0 to about 31 kPa) is a continuous band of overlapping markers that cannot be counted or separated (see log.md). EDS (Table 2): C 62.13, N 37.41, Na 0.46 wt%; Na is residue of the NaCl activating agent. No surface area or pore volume is printed for this sample (the text values 279 m2/g and 0.0035-0.17 cm3/g are not assigned to a sample; see log.md). Basis: paper calls the data 'excess amount of hydrogen adsorbed' (p. 266) without defining it. wt% defined by Eq. (2), p. 267: wt% = hydrogen adsorbed (mol/g) x molar mass of H2 / mass of AC (g) x 100 (sorbent mass only in the denominator, i.e. W1). Degassing (p. 262): dried at 80 C for 12 h in an oven, then degassed under vacuum for 24 h (VacPrep 061); degassing temperature not stated. Sample mass for the H2 measurement not stated (Table 1 'Sample weight (grams)' is the product weight after carbonization, not stored). Acknowledgements credit Prof. Eric May and Dr. Ehsan Sadeghi Pouya for access to the hydrogen adsorption equipment (no institution printed; neither is a co-author), so measuring_lab_id is the corresponding author's group. Composition by EDS (Table 2, weight %), coded dopant_concentration_method = other. Interlayer spacing 0.355 nm (2-theta = 25 deg) is stated once for the samples collectively ('All five samples ... exhibit similar peaks').
basis_evidence: The raw data are obtained in the excess amount of hydrogen adsorbed and is normalized per mass of the adsorbent (mmol g-1) [80].
measuring_lab_id: Salim group, Swinburne University of Technology

Fig. 10 isotherm measured on the 'automated Sievert's PCT Pro instrument' (manufacturer not named), 77 K, up to 5192 kPa; plotted values are averages of three measurements, each on new sample, with error bars (not digitized). BET area 579.4 m2/g (Abstract, Table 3; Conclusion: 'BET surface area of 579 m2 g-1' for 40 % NaCl), N2 at 77 K on a TriStar II, degassed 300 C 12 h; BET P/P0 range not stated. Total pore volume 0.340 cm3/g from Abstract and Section 4.2 (method not stated); Table 3 prints 'Pore Volume' 0.204 cm3/g for the same sample (conflict, 0.340 stored as the value called total). Average pore size 2.35 nm printed without its method (PSD by BJH in the same paragraph; the value equals 4V/A from 0.340 cm3/g and 579.4 m2/g), so pore_diameter_method = unspecified. Basis: paper calls the data 'excess amount of hydrogen adsorbed' (p. 266) without defining it. wt% defined by Eq. (2), p. 267: wt% = hydrogen adsorbed (mol/g) x molar mass of H2 / mass of AC (g) x 100 (sorbent mass only in the denominator, i.e. W1). Degassing (p. 262): dried at 80 C for 12 h in an oven, then degassed under vacuum for 24 h (VacPrep 061); degassing temperature not stated. Sample mass for the H2 measurement not stated (Table 1 'Sample weight (grams)' is the product weight after carbonization, not stored).
